Five failing-before/passing-after regressions cover durable retry rotation and fail-closed attempt recording; candidate order uses the existing last-updated timestamp while the original retry deadline is unchanged. Full local suite: 539 files / 5,348 tests. This does not certify real Stripe behavior or fairness during database contention. Local regression reproduced fresh Stripe submission with a negative budget counter after candidate selection; worker now rejects it and atomically requires a nonnegative counter. Simulated Stripe tests also cover competing claims, exact-cap admission and serializable conflicts; actual Stripe acceptance remains unverified. Two SQL regressions reproduce one workspace crowding another out of a bounded batch. Candidate ranking now interleaves tenant positions before LIMIT, preserving eligibility and retry rotation. This is batch distribution, not durable cross-batch starvation freedom; backoff, representative load and actual Stripe acceptance remain open. A barrier-based regression reproduced duplicate provider calls from the same observed attempt count. The marker now compares and increments that count, deferring the loser; missing/invalid counts block. | R15-003 / historical proposal / future vision | The cloud infrastructure management industry is undergoing a structural transformation. For the past fifteen years, the dominant paradigm has been *human-driven operations assisted by dashboards and alerts.* Engineers monitor metrics, interpret anomalies, formulate remediation plans, seek approval, execute changes, and verify outcomes.
